meanings: Orvenna: the pair-name of Ormund and Penna, the wall-masters of the Keep
derivation: canon formation, as Halyna, Aldwena and Idrenna (orrowen_v2 §3.10): ormund + penna + -a (pair-name: Or- + softened Penn- (p > v) + the lintel -a); the cradle-names are NOTES only (notes_v3 §2.2); the foreword ('Orvenna, our wall-masters, never raise their voices'); unit S01 (wf12)

meanings: Enrella: the pair-name of Enno and Della, the youngest pair of the guild
derivation: canon formation, as Idrenna (orrowen_v2 §3.10): enno + della + -a (pair-name: En- + softened Dell- (d > r) + the lintel -a); the foreword ('Of Enrella, the youngest'); unit S01 (wf12)

meanings: Wendhessa: the pair-name of Wendel and Tessa, the archivists of Eldhythe
derivation: canon formation (orrowen_v2 §3.10): wendel + tessa + -a (pair-name: Wen- + softened Tess- (t > dh) + the lintel -a); the cradle-names are NOTES only (notes_v3 §2.2); the foreword ('under the seal of Wendhessa'); unit S01 (wf12)

meanings: Ebba: a name (old Ebba of Fenholm, who first said the hearth's answer). Names are names
derivation: a name: names are names (no sense given); class B (last full vowel a); after a softening trigger it is unchanged (a vowel); the foreword (Ebba hemm Sedhnell, 'old Ebba of Fenholm'), and I.5, V.5, VI.3; unit S01 (wf12)

meanings: the day of the banner: the day the torn cloak was raised on the wall (the hinge of the Book's clock); dem hedh orl et movenn, 'until the dusk of the day of the banner'
derivation: a construct: canon orl 'a day' + et the + reserve movenn 'a banner, a sign flown' (O1429), the definite possessor; after the article nothing mutates, so movenn keeps its m; the head of a construct takes no article (orrowen_v2 §3.2). The foreword ('till Halyna turned it at dusk on the day of the banner'); unit S01 (wf12)

meanings: the wall-masters ('the master-pair of the wall'): Orvenna's office at the Keep
derivation: a construct: tier-3 prassyanna 'a master-pair' (O1979: prass + S ganna) + et the + canon hald 'wall', the definite possessor; a pair-name is set beside it in apposition (Orvenna, prassyanna et hald). Not *ol brassyanna ('our master-pair': ol beds the p): the wall is the Keep's own, and 'our' is the reader's. The foreword; unit S01 (wf12)
